title: FAU Science Pioneers Quantum Computing Fellowships for FAU High School Scholars
excerpt: The Charles E. Schmidt College of Science’s Machine Perception and Cognitive Robotics (MPCR) Laboratory launched a pilot quantum computing fellowship this summer for select dual-enrolled FAU High School students.

calendar_today Thursday, Nov 19, 2026

The Charles E. Schmidt College of Science’s Machine Perception and Cognitive Robotics (MPCR) Laboratory launched a pilot quantum computing fellowship this summer for select dual-enrolled FAU High School students. Housed within the Gruber AI Sandbox in the S.E. Wimberly Library at FAU’s Boca Raton campus, the program provided three students with hands-on experience using quantum annealing hardware for real-world optimization research.

The fellowship gave students the same tools, infrastructure and hardware access used in the MPCR Lab’s own peer-reviewed research, along with D-Wave Quantum Inc. Leap API credentials. Such access allowed the students to work directly with production quantum annealing hardware, rather than simulations — access typically reserved for graduate level scholars — if at all.

Between May and August, fellows Arielle Fishman, Yaer Peretz and Miriam Kamel identified an original research problem; formulated it as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model; and benchmarked their solutions using D-Wave’s Ocean SDK across simulated annealing, hybrid servers and direct quantum hardware. With direct mentorship, all fellows completed the full arc of the research process, including a literature review, experimental design, statistical analysis and scientific writing, which culminated in individual capstone papers — the initial step toward scientific publication.

The timing of the fellowship’s first cohort places MPCR’s work at the forefront of a major institutional shift. In January 2026, FAU signed an agreement with D-Wave Quantum Inc. to acquire and install the revolutionary Advantage2 system on the university’s Boca Raton campus later this year. The milestone agreement makes FAU the first university in Florida to publicly host a large-scale quantum computer onsite.

The partnership is jointly spearheaded by FAU’s Schmidt College of Science and College of Engineering and Computer Science. The system, which features more than 4,400 qubits, will provide researchers and students with direct access to quantum hardware capable of addressing complex optimization and modeling challenges that are not tractable for classical computing systems.

D-Wave will relocate its new corporate headquarters to the Boca Raton Innovation Center, creating a key U.S. hub for quantum technology development. This partnership positions FAU as a center for quantum education and innovation, attracts industry and investment, and prepares the next generation of technology leaders to tackle problems beyond the reach of classical computers.

Summer 2026 MPCR Lab/FAU High Quantum Computing Fellows

Arielle Fishman

Project: Office Fire Evacuation Routing
Description: Modeling building evacuation as a graph optimization problem — assigning each room of a 12‑room, 100‑occupant office building to an exit to minimize evacuation distance while accounting for hallway and doorway congestion, benchmarked against classical Dijkstra/A* routing across four solvers.

Yaer Peretz

Project: Mars Habitat Crisis Power Allocation
Description: Allocating limited power across a Mars habitat's critical systems during an emergency, such as a dust storm, modeling allocation under scarcity as a resource‑allocation QUBO with conflict, dependency and mandatory‑system constraints.

Miriam Kamel

Project: Electroencephalogram (EEG) Feature Selection for Brain‑Computer Interfaces
Description: Selecting the most discriminative frequency‑band features for classifying left‑vs. right‑hand motor imagery in a brain‑computer interface, formulated as a redundancy‑aware QUBO and benchmarked against a real motor‑imagery EEG dataset spanning 11 subjects.
